trust_decision.summary: cmd.cgi decides whether to commit an external command by comparing the NagFormId cookie with the nagFormId form field (double-submit), fail-closed unless cgi_cookie_fail_open; the cookie value may only come from HTTP_COOKIE (getcgi.c filters it out of query/body).

landing_point.why: Only CSRF check in the tree; error string 'Invalid or missing CSRF cookie' at cgi/cmd.c:245 and the double-submit compare sit here.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The listed fix commit changes no security code: only version strings and dates (fix.diff:13-16, fix.diff:69-79, fix.diff:104-107, fix.diff:143-148). The pinned tree already carries the 4.5.14 CSRF-cookie changelog entry (Changelog:5-10) and the hardened cookie handling (cgi/getcgi.c:227-231, cgi/getcgi.c:264-278).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is no published fix to scope against. A solver could argue the code is already patched, because the changelog for this release says so (Changelog:10).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: cgi_cookie_fail_open=1 must keep letting third-party integrations commit commands without the cookie; the read-only JSON CGIs must keep accepting and ignoring the NagFormId cookie.

O7_producer.where: Token producer is set_cookie() at cgi/cmd.c:285-299, which the check uses directly; it is a handler, not a separate schema or cache layer.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: CSRF token is produced with rand() and no srand() anywhere under cgi/, so the double-submit value may be predictable
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The token generator is not the comparison logic the report points at, and 'the cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict' (cgi/cmd.c:298).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Cookie lookup uses strstr("NagFormId=") on the raw Cookie header, so a cookie whose name only ends in NagFormId also matches (parser differential on the token's identity)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Exploiting it needs cookie injection from a sibling origin, which a solver could treat as a separate threat model.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: GET/HEAD path that re-admits a NagFormId pair from QUERY_STRING via a second parse path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getcgivars() has separate GET and POST input branches, and a maintainer adding a method-override or legacy path could skip the filter at getcgi.c:227.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: cmd.c's own variable parser accepts a NagFormId name from any source pair, so a new cookie-like source (e.g. a header) appended to pairlist would bypass the cookie-only rule
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The cookie value is pushed into the same pairlist as form variables (cgi/getcgi.c:270), so cmd.c cannot tell where it came from.

O10_build.language: C (CGIs); PHP only for the html/ front pages
services: CGI-capable web server (Apache) for end-to-end tests; CGIs can be driven by env vars REQUEST_METHOD, QUERY_STRING and HTTP_COOKIE
O10_build.project_tests: No CGI or CSRF tests found; tests exist only for lib/ (e.g. lib/test-squeue.c).

j.j_sites_touched: none (fix commit touches only configure, configure.ac, spec files, doxy.conf, html/main.php and html/side.php version strings, include/common.h, startup/default-service.in, update-version)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten the strcmp at cgi/cmd.c:225 or reject a missing cookie, without touching token generation or cookie-name parsing.
